en.html:
Zeniarai Benten was a peculiar shrine inside a cave. Wash your money in the spring at the back, they said, and the amount would double. Bhagwan, very generous. The entire concept of earning money, however, was now in difficulty.

Around this financial miracle, the houses were mostly modest. Seedha bol: poor-looking. Dried-out wooden houses, all of them. One matchstick, and the lane could become altogether too lively.

Ritsu's family ran a small general store among them. Household necessities, food, stationery—whatever you needed for getting through an ordinary day, they generally had it. That shop closed, and half your daily life would have to stand outside waiting.

Business was good enough to let their daughter spend her time playing. If she really started playing, though, some loan shark would have the shop as security within three days. Beti enjoying, shop mortgaged. Such happiness the family could not afford.

That level of recreation was for a company president's young master, with buildings along the coastal line. Not for the general-store class of citizen.

We contributed to the shop's prosperity too. Already cheap, then a friends' discount on top—why should we drag ourselves to the supermarket on the main road? And when they generously handed over the leftovers, even that question became unnecessary.

Only, one small consideration.

銭洗弁天とは洞窟の中にある変わったお社で、その
奥の湧き水でお金を洗うと倍になるというありがたい
ような色々ぶち壊しのようなご利益で知られている。

　そのわりに、近隣の家は慎ましい造りのものが多く、
より素直に言えば貧乏くさい。
　マッチ一本でとても楽しいことになりそうなくらい
枯れた木造建築ばかりだ。

　リツの家はその中で小さな雑貨屋を営んでいる。
　生活用品を中心に食品、文房具など、日常的に必要
となる物品全般を取り扱っているので、その重宝ぶり
たるや只事ではない。

　娘を遊ばせておけるのは店が充分に繁盛していれば
こそだった。……といっても、もしリツが<ruby>本当に<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>遊び
始めたら、雑貨屋は三日でどこかの高利貸しの抵当に
入ってしまうだろうが。

　そんな真似が許されるのは臨海ラインにビルを持つ
社長さんちのご令息くらいに違いない。

　雑貨屋の繁盛にはおれたちも一役買っている。
　もともと安めの値段設定がさらに友達割引されるの
なら、わざわざ大路のスーパーなんぞに足を運ぶ理由
は全くないからだ。

　余り物を気前良くくれたりするとなればなおのこと。
　とはいえ。

en.html:
The wind was cold. I went back over our talk with Ritsu's parents. Neither of them had any real idea.

Yesterday morning she had left for school. Since then, home she had not come.

One full day. Pura din, and nobody knew where she was. This had never happened before. Haan, she played around. Sometimes she stayed out overnight. But every day, family and friends got to see her face. That much she always did.

Normally the difficulty was getting a little less Ritsu. You could not have imagined asking, please, some Ritsu, any quantity will do. Now here we were, and even one glimpse was unavailable.

I had been afraid to say it. Bas, that was the truth.

Say a thing, and it becomes real? Kya nonsense. If my mouth had that power, the first thing out of it would have been 'meat for lunch,' and we would not be discussing anything else until the experiment was complete.

But perhaps the time for hiding behind that fear was already over...

My spine shook the instant I heard it. Quite openly. Sharam? Nahin. For this, no shame at all.

In one sense, what Tadayasu had named was feared and hated even more than Rokuhara in this country.

The Silver Star.

Everybody carried that fear somewhere inside. Abhi? Would it be now? The instant it arrived.

en.html:
Tadayasu"In these conditions, crime not being an everyday affair would be the strange thing. But chalo, let us keep the cases separate."
Tadayasu"Suppose Ritsu has been caught up in a crime. What kind? Assault, murder, kidnapping. Those would be the main possibilities."
Konatsu"..."
Tadayasu"Assault: twenty-four hours with no contact is odd. If she was too badly hurt to get home, the hospital should contact her family."
Tadayasu"Badly hurt, and nobody took her to a hospital... then the next case."
Yuhi"..."
Tadayasu"Murder. But here also, socho. Killing someone is easy. Afterward, the person is dead, but the problem is very much alive. Usually somebody finds out quickly."
Tadayasu"A dead body attracts tremendous notice. In a city like Kamakura, one appearing and nobody noticing for an entire day—that probability should be quite low."

en.html:
'As things stand now,' he added quietly, and stopped.

For a while, only the wind.

His explanation made sense. Tadayasu was not one of those fellows whose genius arrived with lightning and everyone fell backward. But give him the facts: this goes here, this follows that, toh this is the answer. Nobody put things in order better.

Haan, I could follow it. I could accept it. The head had accepted delivery, signed its name, everything.

The rest of me was refusing the parcel. No reason supplied. Just this stupid unease, standing there with folded arms.

Why was it still—

Chhod. Leave it.

My vague feeling against Tadayasu's reasoning: why was I even holding a contest? Compare exam marks. My magnificent guesswork achieved roughly half his score. Half the marks, and now I wanted equal voting rights.

So Tadayasu was right. She would come home while we were worrying here. Zaroor.

I decided to believe that and lifted the carton to my mouth.

Yuhi"Yes. And?"
Konatsu"And what?"
Yuhi"'And why are you in my room, crawling into my futon?' This is the meaning of 'And?' Full question was there. You have chosen not to hear it."
